messages:
Priya (Customer): Hey team — our production app started getting 429s around 10:40 UTC and latency spiked. Using Dedicated pool ABC-42. Not seeing any quota alerts in console. Example response header: `x-rw-error: rate_limit_exceeded` and body `Too many requests`. Any ideas?
Alex (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Priya. Can you paste the root request ID from one of the 429s? Also which model + route?
Priya (Customer): root_id=01FZQZ6R1, model=rw-large-v1, route=/v1/generate, region=us-west-2. We sent a brief traffic spike (spike from 50 rps -> ~600 rps for ~90s) after a marketing email.
Sam (SRE): Thanks. On Dedicated pools we enforce a throughput cap tied to the reserved capacity and the pool's token bucket. A sustained spike like that can exhaust the burst budget and then enforce per-route throttles. Do you have `burst_capacity` configured on the pool?
Priya (Customer): I don't think we touched pool config after onboarding. How do I check?
Alex (Support): You can see pool config in Console > Dedicated > Pools > ABC-42, or `redwoodctl get pool ABC-42 --output yaml`. If easier, paste the pool id and I can pull it.
Priya (Customer): pasted. Pasting the small curl I ran: ```bash
curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=rw-large-v1" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Marta (Eng - Runtime): Quick note: there are two separate rate limit surfaces — global account-level QPS (smoothing layer) and the pool-level throughput cap (reserved pool token bucket). The smoothing policy may throttle short spikes to preserve tail latencies for other customers on shared infra. But since you're Dedicated, the pool cap should be dominant. If the pool's cached tokens were exhausted by the spike, subsequent requests are 429'd until refill.
Jules (Eng - Platform): I'm pulling metrics for ABC-42. I see a ~10x spike starting 10:39:12 UTC and a token bucket drain that reached zero at 10:40:45. Refill rate is set to 200 qps for the pool and `burst_capacity` is 1200 tokens. Your observed sustained 600 rps would exceed refill and drain the bucket in ~2s, then 429s.
Priya (Customer): So why didn't we get an alert? Our alert was set to 10% remaining tokens.
Sam (SRE): Alerts are per-pool but there's an alerting window; short fast drains can happen before the alert fires if the burn rate is high. Also check that the alerting subscription isn't paused.
Alex (Support): Two immediate mitigations: 1) apply a short client-side backoff/retry with jitter to smooth the spike; 2) ask for a temporary increase to pool refill or burst capacity while you investigate marketing schedule. We can open an emergency change.
Priya (Customer): For the short term we'll add exponential backoff. How do we request the temporary increase?
Jules (Eng - Platform): I can submit a provisioning change. Need approval from Eng-runtime for safety and confirmation of billing tier. ETA ~30m. Can we confirm: you want target sustained 600 qps for 5 minutes starting now?
Priya (Customer): Yes, for next 60 minutes if possible.
Marta (Eng - Runtime): We need to validate headroom on the host pools. Two options: bump pool refill to 700 qps (safe) or increase burst_capacity to 3000 to absorb the spike. Bumping refill affects allocation and billing. Given it's a short blast, increasing burst_capacity is lower risk.
Sam (SRE): Also check route-level per-client QPS. We have per-route fairness that could still enforce a hard cap per API key. If your app opened many concurrent connections, per-key frontend limits might be hit (X-Per-Key-Limit). Send one affected request header dump.
Priya (Customer): Here's headers from 1 failed response: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-error: rate_limit_exceeded
x-rw-retry-after: 3
x-rw-pool-id: ABC-42
x-rw-request-id: 01FZQZ6R1\``` 
Alex (Support): `x-rw-retry-after: 3` suggests the runtime asked the client to wait 3s. That's consistent with a drained token bucket.
Marta (Eng - Runtime): Action plan I'm proposing: 1) temporary burst_capacity bump to 3000 on ABC-42 (no long-term billing change), 2) enable a short smoothing window tweak so frontend allows a higher per-key instantaneous rate for the next hour, 3) set an alert to fire at 50% token level for 10s window.
Jules (Eng - Platform): I've queued the pool change request (REQ-8241). Approval needed from Runtime (Marta).
Marta (Eng - Runtime): Approved. I'll kick off the change. Deploy-bot: patch rollout to platform-config/v2 smoothing policy.
deploy-bot: Started rollout 2024-11-03T10:48:30Z -> config:v2.5.4 with canary 10%
Marta (Eng - Runtime): Patch applied to smoothing policy. Pool burst_capacity bumped. Can you retry now, Priya?
Priya (Customer): Retried at 10:49:25 UTC — spike replayed, no 429s this time, latency back to normal. Thanks! :tada:
Alex (Support): Great. Follow-ups: - We'll keep the temporary bump for 1 hour then revert. - Recommend customer throttle in client (100ms jittered backoff) and a pre-warm for planned blasts. - I'll open a follow-up doc with recommended alert thresholds and a playbook.
Priya (Customer): Thanks everyone. Please confirm when the bump is reverted.
Marta (Eng - Runtime): Reverting in 60m unless you ask to extend. I'll add notes to REQ-8241 and create a short KB for prewarming dedicated pools.
Sam (SRE): FYI: we'll also add a short-term metric to track token bucket drain rates > 5x refill to catch this earlier.
Alex (Support): Closing the thread for now, moving to follow-up ticket support/REQ-8241. Thanks all.
